C0.quote: Motivated by recent work in computational social choice
C0.note: Borderline. Agents report rankings over other agents, which are aggregated into a choice of k centres. The paper motivates this as representative election within the metric distortion framework, so I code ELIG under the doubt rule.

C1.quote: using at most O(k 2 ) overall distance evaluations, obtain a 2-distortion
C1.note: Every main result is a distortion bound, either an upper bound achieved by an algorithm under query or centre budgets, or a lower bound. The lower bounds are information-theoretic rather than computational, so WD covers the largest share and AL is secondary.
